chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When one of you is constrained (in wealth), let him inform his brother, and he should not support himself (by hiding his need).

key_terms.يُعِينُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ: To support oneself (often implying hiding need or maintaining false independence)

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do when facing financial constraint according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the virtue of modest vulnerability, encouraging believers to share their burdens with trusted companions rather than isolating themselves in shame. It underscores the communal responsibility to support one another, framing financial ease as a shared state rather than a solitary achievement. This guidance fosters social cohesion and mutual aid, key tenets of Shia ethical life.
